title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Operating Procedures, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Jordan Alvarez
body:
Overview:

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standard approach to authoring, publishing, operating, and triaging developer-facing documentation in the Developer Experience (DevEx) area. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the list of top support issues with their canonical fixes. The goal is a consistent, discoverable, and high-quality docs surface that scales with product changes and reduces support load.

Audience:
- DevEx engineers and technical writers who author SDK guides and API examples.
- Product and engineering owners who approve and ship changes.
- Support and solutions engineers who rely on canonical fixes and troubleshooting steps.

Ownership and roles:
- Owner: eng-developer-experience (DevEx team)
- Primary author(s): DevEx technical writers / SDK engineers
- Reviewers: Product engineers, Security reviewer where applicable, Support lead for top-issue validation
- Publisher: Docs release engineer (rotating oncall from DevEx)

Scope and doc types (this playbook applies to):
- SDK Guides: language-specific reference guides (Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, Java) and migration notes when SDK changes are breaking.
- Quickstarts & Templates: one-page quickstarts for typical flows (chat integration, embeddings, streaming responses) and repository templates for projects.
- API Examples: short, copy-paste examples for common tasks (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, tool/function calling).
- Docs Site Operating Procedures: CI checks, commit conventions, release cadence, and emergency patch workflows.
- Top Support Issues: canonical triage and fixes for the most frequent support tickets seen in the last 12 months.

Standards and style (must-follow):
- Complete sentence prose with clear headings and short intro.
- Include a one-line summary at the top of each page.
- Provide runnable examples for SDKs and a cURL fallback.
- All code examples MUST specify the SDK version and a minimal requirements block.
- Link to related pages and the API reference (stable canonical URL).
- Use the following metadata on every page: title, summary (one line), author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated, reviewers (if any), labels (0-8).

Template: Quickstart (recommended structure)
1) One-line summary
2) Prerequisites (API key, SDK version, region)
3) Install steps (CLI/pip/npm)
4) Minimal example (copy-paste runnable)
5) Common parameters and recommended defaults
6) Next steps & related links

Example quickstart snippet (Python):
# Quickstart: text generation (Redwood Python SDK v0.8.x)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-2.1", prompt="Write a haiku about latency.", max_tokens=40)
print(resp.text)

API Example guidelines:
- Provide both SDK and cURL examples.
- Show streaming examples when applicable and explain behavior (chunking, stop tokens).
- Document any rate-limit or quota behavior for the endpoint.

Docs site CI / release procedures (operating procedures):
1) Branching and PRs
   - All doc changes submit a PR to the docs repo using `docs/` prefix branch names (e.g., docs/sdk-python-0.8-upgrade).
   - PR must include a short changelog entry (one-line) and updated metadata block.
2) Automated checks (pre-merge)
   - Lint: prose linting (spelling, grammar), link validation, code-block language tagging.
   - Build: static site build (preview) must succeed in CI.
   - Examples smoke test: run Python/Node quickstart examples against a sandbox project to validate imports/compile.
3) Review and approvals
   - At least one peer reviewer from DevEx and one reviewer from the owning product team for API changes.
   - Security review required for pages that mention internal endpoints, tokens, or PII handling.
4) Publish cadence
   - Minor doc fixes: weekly (automated publish on Fridays at 06:00 UTC).
   - Major / breaking changes: coordinated release with product release notes, gated by the release manager.
5) Emergency docs patch
   - If a live docs page contains a critical bug (security, wrong API example causing data loss), open a high-priority PR and tag @docs-oncall. The oncall engineer can fast-track merge after a brief triage and post a follow-up changelog note.

Canonical SDK guide checklist (before publishing):
- [ ] SDK version header and compatibility table present
- [ ] One minimal example that runs in <1 minute
- [ ] Pagination, error handling, and retry guidance included
- [ ] Notes on configuration defaults and environment variables (REGION, API_KEY)
- [ ] Triage section: common errors and suggested fixes

Top support issues (tracked, triaged, canonical fixes)
- Issue: Authentication failure with 401 when using env var
  - Symptoms: SDK returns 401 on every request after onboarding.
  - Root causes: Token copy/paste includes stray quotes or env var not exported in shell.
  - Canonical fix: Verify API key is set `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` (no quotes), run `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | sed -n '1p'` and run `redwood-cli whoami` to validate. Update quickstart with exact export examples for bash/zsh/powershell.
- Issue: Streaming responses hang for >2s before first chunk
  - Symptoms: Client receives no chunks until final event or timeout.
  - Root causes: Missing `stream=True` flag in SDK call or firewall/proxy buffering.
  - Canonical fix: Add explicit `stream=True` in examples and document common proxy settings (disable buffering for SSE). Provide curl example with `-N` to disable buffering.
- Issue: Large-embedding requests fail with 413 Payload Too Large
  - Symptoms: Embedding creation requests for >16,384 tokens fail.
  - Root causes: Customers attempt to embed long documents in a single request.
  - Canonical fix: Recommend chunking strategy, provide Python helper `chunk_text_for_embeddings()` in SDK examples, and call out model/token limits in quickstarts.
- Issue: Unexpected high token usage after prompt templating
  - Symptoms: Customers report billing spike due to long prompts.
  - Root causes: Prompt templates include repeated system messages or untrimmed examples.
  - Canonical fix: Add a prompt-cost checklist and an example of compact system messages; show how to use `max_prompt_length` sanitizer before sending to API.

Troubleshooting playbook (triage flow):
1) Reproduce with minimal example from docs. If reproducible, attach sanitized request/response to ticket.
2) Check client SDK version and region compatibility.
3) Run smoke tests against sandbox account and collect logs (request_id, timestamp, latency).
4) Escalation: if issue is production-impacting (SLA failure, data loss), open an incident in the oncall channel and link to docs page for mitigation steps.

Maintenance and metrics:
- Owner should review top 10 doc pages monthly for accuracy.
- Metrics to track: page views, time-to-first-byte for example downloads, support ticket volume referencing docs, and number of doc-related incidents.
- Quarterly: a DevEx doc audit (accuracy, API compatibility, security review) with results published to eng-platform.

Appendix: Recommended metadata table for SDK guides (as text)
| Field | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| title | Python SDK: Text Generation | One-line title as H1 |
| summary | Quickstart and reference for text generation using Python SDK v0.8.x | One-line summary under title |
| sdk_version | v0.8.2 | Required for reproducibility |
| languages | ["python"] | Languages covered (list) |
| last_tested | 2026-02-10 | Date when examples were last smoke-tested |

Related resources:
- API reference (stable): https://api.redwood.inference/reference
- DevEx repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex-docs
- Sandbox project for example validation: internal link to sandbox project
